shipping-address.interface.ts: IShippingAddress extends IShippingAddressEditable and adds only id, so the field list is defined once

IOrder declares both shippingAddressId: number | null and shippingAddress: IShippingAddress, and IShippingAddress has its own id: a minor duplication of identity
IOrderEditable.items is typed IOrderItem[] and not an editable item type, unlike shippingAddress: IShippingAddressEditable: a minor inconsistency

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All three files cover one concern: the data shape of the Order aggregate. order.interface.ts declares IOrder and IOrderEditable and uses IOrderItem from order-item.interface.ts and IShippingAddress / IShippingAddressEditable from shipping-address.interface.ts. Order, OrderItem and ShippingAddress implement these interfaces. The files contain only types and no logic, so no rule or invariant is coded twice and nothing goes around the module's abstractions.

Minor points that do not fail the rubric:
- IOrder has both shippingAddressId and shippingAddress, and IShippingAddress already carries its own id. The same identity is stored twice.
- IOrderItem stores lineTotal, and IOrder stores subtotal and totalPrice, all of which can be derived from other fields. Nothing here calculates them, so no calculation is repeated.
- The editable pattern is applied unevenly. IOrderEditable uses IShippingAddressEditable but takes the full IOrderItem, including id and lineTotal, because there is no IOrderItemEditable.
- The path comment at the top of order.interface.ts is out of date.

None of these splits the module into unrelated concerns or repeats a rule in more than one place.
